questions.q: How did Josiah keep the Passover in Jerusalem?
questions.a: He had the Passover lambs killed and placed the priests in their positions in the house of Yahweh.

questions.q: Where did Josiah tell the people to put the holy ark instead of carrying it on their shoulders?
questions.a: They were told to put the holy ark in the house that Solomon built.

questions.q: How were the people to get ready for the Passover?
questions.a: The people were to kill the Passover lambs and consecrate themselves in obedience to God’s word.

questions.q: How did the people of Israel offer their sacrifices to Yahweh?
questions.a: They killed the Passover lamb, splashed the blood, skinned the lambs, and offered the burnt offerings to Yahweh, as was written in the book of Moses.

questions.q: What did the people of Israel do after the Passover celebration?
questions.a: They celebrated the Festival of Unleavened Bread for seven days.

questions.q: Why was this celebration of the Passover so special?
questions.a: It was special because this is the first time it had been held in Israel since the days of the prophet Samuel.

questions.q: What was the message that the king of Egypt brought to Josiah?
questions.a: He said God had commanded him to fight against Carchemish and that Josiah should not interfere.

questions.q: What was Josiah’s reaction to the message from the king of Egypt?
questions.a: He did not listen to the king’s words, but instead, Josiah disguised himself so he could fight.

questions.q: What happened to Josiah on the battle field?
questions.a: He was shot by archers and his servants took him to Jerusalem, where he later died.

questions.q: What are the songs of lament that have become customary in Israel?
questions.a: They are songs that have been sung to lament for Josiah and are still sung.

questions.q: Where are the matters of Josiah and his good deeds recorded?
questions.a: They are contained in The Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.

commentary.text: Verses 1–19 The destruction Josiah made of idolatry, was more largely related in the book of Kings. His solemnizing the passover is related here. The Lord's supper resembles the passover more than any other of the Jewish festivals; and the due observance of that ordinance, is a proof of growing piety and devotion. God alone can truly make our hearts holy, and prepare them for his holy services; but there are duties belonging to us, in doing which we obtain this blessing from the Lord.

The Scripture does not condemn Josiah's conduct in opposing Pharaoh. Yet Josiah seems to deserve blame for not inquiring of the Lord after he was warned; his death might be a rebuke for his rashness, but it was a judgment on a hypocritical and wicked people. He that lives a life of repentance, faith, and obedience, cannot be affected by the sudden manner in which he is removed. The people lamented him. Many mourn over sufferings, who will not forsake the sins that caused God to send them. Yet this alone can turn away judgments. If we blame Josiah's conduct, we should be watchful, lest we be cut down in a way dishonourable to our profession.
